title: Ship it: into a container, with none of your machine in it
note: 55% dead picture on the sharp detector - much of this lecture is the running console, which is genuinely moving and is left alone. Six cutaways, 80s of 212s (38%). No sync leads at all.

inserts.why: Names the lecture and the argument in its first sentence, over a static editor.

slides.stamp: with none of your machine in it

slides.kicker: running on your own machine is not shipping
slides.wrong: it works on my machine, so it works
slides.right: your Node is the right version and your folder is where it expects to be
slides.note: and stop the local server first, or the thing that answers is the old process

inserts.why: The Dockerfile read line by line. On the frame it is small text in an editor pane.

slides.kicker: a Dockerfile a teammate wrote without being asked

rows.t: a published Node image, and a working directory
the package file, then the source
drops to an unprivileged user, exposes the port, runs the server

slides.kicker: and there is no install step anywhere in it
slides.wrong: every Dockerfile needs an install step
slides.right: the project has no dependencies, so the build fetches nothing beyond the base image
slides.note: and it works with the network unplugged once that image is cached

inserts.why: The moment the project changes category, and the layers it changes through.

slides.kicker: watch the layers go past, because this is the moment
four steps, most of them already cached
slides.caption: no dependency resolution, and no lock file to reconcile

inserts.why: The payoff of the zero-dependency rule, over a build log that has finished scrolling. Ends four seconds into the next sentence so the docker run command arrives with its own words rather than ahead of them.

slides.kicker: and notice what is not happening in that build
slides.wrong: a Dockerfile needs an install step
slides.right: no dependency resolution, no lock file, nothing fetched beyond the base image
slides.note: it builds with the network unplugged once that image is cached

slides.kicker: that zero-dependency rule looked like an aesthetic choice on day one
slides.stamp: a folder on this laptop is now an artefact

inserts.why: The port mapping, which the narration says matters more than it looks and which the frame shows as one flag.

slides.kicker: eight zero nine zero outside, eight zero eight zero in

nodes.sub: wherever I decide to put it
where the app still believes it is

slides.kicker: and that is the whole promise of an image

inserts.why: The only check worth making, and what its answer proves.

slides.kicker: curl it, and ask for the status code
and nothing of my machine is in that reply

inserts.why: The close of the week, over a committed repository that has stopped changing.

slides.kicker: and that is the week's work in one repository

rows.t: a test suite that was made to mean something
a tool we wrote ourselves to run other agents
and an image that carries all of it somewhere else

slides.kicker: and it took one working day
